It may be that what is meant is what he endures and suffers of hardships in this world, in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and on the Day when the witnesses stand, and that he should strive in an action that relieves him of these hardships and brings him lasting joy and happiness; and if he does not do so, he will continue to endure severe punishment forever and ever. Rather, Allah has seen him, preserved his deeds for him, and assigned to him the Noble Recording Angels for everything he did of good and evil.

{8–10} Then He reminded him of His blessings, saying: {Did We not make for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips?} For beauty, sight, speech and other essential benefits in them; these are the blessings of this world. Then He said, concerning the blessings of religion: {And We guided him to the two paths (najdayn)}; that is, the paths of good and evil; We made clear to him guidance from error and right direction from misguidance. {11} But this human being did not do that; {so he has not attempted the steep path ('aqabah)}; that is, he has not plunged into it and crossed over it, because he follows his desire, and this ascent is difficult for him.

{1–3} Allah the Exalted swears by {this city} (the secure one), which is Makkah the Honoured, the best of cities absolutely, especially at the time when the Messenger (ﷺ) resided in it, and by {the begetter and what he begot}; that is, Adam and his offspring.

{4–7} The thing sworn to is His saying: {Verily, We have created man in toil (kabad)}. It may be that what is meant is what he endures and suffers of hardships in this world, in the barzakh (the intermediate state), and on the Day when the witnesses stand, and that he should strive in an action that relieves him of these hardships and brings him lasting joy and happiness; and if he does not do so, he will continue to endure severe punishment forever and ever. It may also be that the meaning is: We have created man in the best form and the most upright constitution, able to act and to perform strenuous works, yet despite that he has not thanked Allah for this great blessing, but has become insolent through well-being and has become arrogant toward his Creator. Through his ignorance and wrongdoing he supposes that this state will last for him and that the authority of his power will never be removed. Therefore He said: {Does he suppose that no one has power over him?} He transgresses and boasts of the wealth he has spent on the desires of his soul, so he says: {I have squandered wealth in abundance (lubadan)}; that is, much of it piled upon much. Allah called spending on desires and sins "squandering" because the one who spends gains nothing from what he has spent, and nothing returns to him from his spending except regret, loss, weariness and poverty; unlike one who spends seeking the pleasure of Allah in the way of good, for he has traded with Allah and gained many times over what he spent. Allah, threatening this one who boasted of what he spent on desires, said: {Does he suppose that no one has seen him?}; that is, does he imagine in this act of his that Allah does not see him and will not call him to account for the small and the great? Rather, Allah has seen him, preserved his deeds for him, and assigned to him the Noble Recording Angels for everything he did of good and evil.

{8–10} Then He reminded him of His blessings, saying: {Did We not make for him two eyes, and a tongue and two lips?} For beauty, sight, speech and other essential benefits in them; these are the blessings of this world. Then He said, concerning the blessings of religion: {And We guided him to the two paths (najdayn)}; that is, the paths of good and evil; We made clear to him guidance from error and right direction from misguidance. These abundant favours require of the servant that he fulfil the rights of Allah and thank Him for His blessings, and that he not use them to disobey Allah.

{11} But this human being did not do that; {so he has not attempted the steep path ('aqabah)}; that is, he has not plunged into it and crossed over it, because he follows his desire, and this ascent is difficult for him.

{12–16} Then He explained this 'aqabah by His saying: {The freeing of a slave}; that is, freeing him from bondage by manumitting him or helping him to pay his contract of emancipation (kitabah), and a fortiori the ransoming of a Muslim captive among the disbelievers; {or feeding on a day of severe hunger (masghabah)}; that is, in a time of great famine, by feeding the most needy of people at the time of need; {an orphan near of kin (dha maqrabah)}; that is, one who combines being an orphan with being poor and a relative; {or a needy person in misery (dha matrabah)}; that is, one who has been pressed down into the dust by need and necessity.

{17} {Then he is among those who believed}: and did righteous deeds; that is, they believed in their hearts in what must be believed, and did righteous deeds with their limbs, and this includes every obligatory or recommended word and action. {And enjoined one another to patience}: in obedience to Allah, in abstaining from disobedience, and in bearing His painful decrees; by urging one another to submit to these and to perform them fully, with the breast expanded and the soul at rest. {And enjoined one another to compassion}: toward creation; by giving to the needy among them, teaching their ignorant, attending to what they need in every respect, helping them in their religious and worldly interests, and loving for them what one loves for oneself and disliking for them what one dislikes for oneself.

{18} {Those}: who have upheld these attributes, whom Allah has enabled to cross {this} 'aqabah. {Those are the companions of the right hand (maymanah)}: because they discharged what Allah commanded of His rights and the rights of His servants, and abstained from what they were forbidden; and this is the sign and the mark of happiness.

{19–20} {And those who disbelieved in Our signs}: by casting these matters behind their backs, so they did not believe in Allah, did not affirm Him, did not do righteous deeds, and did not show mercy to the servants of Allah. Those are {the companions of the left hand (mash'amah). Over them is a fire vaulted shut}; that is, closed, {in extended columns}, stretched out behind them, so that its doors will not open, and they will be in constriction, anxiety and severe distress.

And praise be to Allah.
